summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 9. Demonstrated primary failure: stopped node1, verified node2 had zero data loss, promoted node2 to writable primary, repointed node3 to replicate from node2, then rebuilt node1 as a standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 primary, node1/node3 standbys, all data consistent. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes sequentially (standbys first, primary last), proving changed boot_id/uptime and full post-restart health/data/replication recovery on each.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 module on node1, node2, node3 via dnf
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes
Initialized primary database on node1, configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, pg_hba.conf for replication and client access
Created 'repl' replication role with generated password on node1
Created baseline test table public.bench with data
Created physical replication slots node2_slot/node3_slot on node1; ran pg_basebackup with -R on node2 and node3 to become standbys
Verified streaming replication healthy (pg_stat_replication) and data present on both standbys
Inserted a pre-failover committed row and confirmed it replicated to standbys before disruption
Stopped postgresql on node1 to simulate primary loss
Verified node2 had the committed row (no data loss), promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote
Wrote new data on node2 as new primary and confirmed it persisted
Created replication slots node3_slot/node1_slot on node2; repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2 via ALTER SYSTEM + restart, verified streaming and data
Rebuilt node1 via pg_basebackup from node2 as a new standby, verified recovery mode and full data set
Confirmed node2 shows both node1 and node3 streaming and slots active
Captured boot_id/uptime/service/data baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node3, then node2 (primary last) via systemctl reboot, polling until exec access returned
Verified new boot_id and uptime on each node after reboot
Verified postgresql active, correct recovery role, and full data set (plus write test on node2) after each reboot
Confirmed both standbys reconnected to node2 in pg_stat_replication and replicated a post-restart write

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2/node3 streaming; both standbys show identical baseline row

evidence.requirement: Failover: primary loss handled without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Committed row inserted on node1, node1 stopped, node2 confirmed to have the row via matching WAL LSN before promotion; node2 promoted and became writable

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to node2 and streaming; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2, joined as standby with full data; node2 shows both node1 and node3 actively streaming

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31949c21...; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); new boot_id b4f16ed8... with new uptime; postgresql active as standby with full 3-row dataset

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 9d397578... new uptime; postgresql active as standby with full dataset

evidence.requirement: node2 (primary) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state incl. quorum/replication
evidence.summary: Baseline: both standbys streaming; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 5acf53b7... new uptime; postgresql active, still primary and writable (new insert succeeded); both standbys reconnected in pg_stat_replication and replicated the new row
